newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's adds three new sandwiches.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's adds three new sandwiches.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. on Thursday launched a new deluxe fish sandwich and two deluxe chicken offerings to complement its four-month-old Arch Deluxe hamburger, which the company says exceeded its expectations.
McDonald's, which operates 19,200 restaurants worldwide, added the new Crispy Chicken Deluxe, Grilled Chicken Deluxe and Fish Filet Deluxe to its U.S. menu.
The new sandwiches, which will replace existing chicken and fish menu items, come on the heels of a splashy multi-million-dollar campaign for its Arch Deluxe, which met with mixed reviews.
Some analysts, pointing to a decline in McDonald's U.S. same store sales, which measure results from units open at least a year, have said the Arch Deluxe was not successful.

"We think it's been enormously successful," McDonald's Vice Chairman Jack Greenberg said of the Arch Deluxe, which was launched in May. "We sold over 100 million (Arch Deluxe) sandwiches in the first month."
He said the introduction of the Arch Deluxe hamburger was 38 percent better than expectations. "And it's still doing over projection," he added in a telephone interview.

McDonald's did not disclose the amount of money it is spending to advertise and promote the Arch Deluxe and the Deluxe line of sandwiches. A spokesman said these promotions are not separate allocations but will come out of McDonald's overall advertising and promotion budget, which in 1995 amounted to about $1.8 billion.

The addition of the new Crispy Chicken Deluxe, Grilled Chicken Deluxe and Fish Filet Deluxe sandwiches in the United States should help increase the size of the average customer check and raise the profit on the menu items.
"The penny profit on these new sandwiches is better," Greenberg said.
